content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a new AL method to adapt to both classification and regression tasks. During training process, they use kalman filter to update the weights of the basic classifier to acclerating training process.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: The proposed kalman-fliter based AL sampling strategy is flexible. It can deal with classification and regularization tasks and also can be intergrated into most existing AL sampling strategies.

Weakness: The experiment part is too weak. No baselines for comparison. No experiments about how to accelerate the training, improving generalization performance and protecting algorithm from over-fitting by using the proposed method on top of existing AL approaches like variance reduction. For classification task, only test on MNIST dataset with one-layer NN, the top accuracy is less than 90% after 800 iterations. In other publications like [r1], the accuracy of MNIST is larger than 95% after 200 labeled instances. Is the proposed method can be used on deeper NNs? If yes, the author should conduct related experiments. If not, the novelty is limited. For regression task, only synthetic experiments with very easy objective formulation is adopted.

[r1] Kirsch A, Van Amersfoort J, Gal Y. Batchbald: Efficient and diverse batch acquisition for deep bayesian active learning[J]. Advances in neural information processing systems, 2019, 32.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: the paper is easy to follow. 

Quality: the experimental part could not tell the effectiveness of their proposed method.

Novelty: the proposed method is novel.

Reproducibility: the author does not provide code for checking the detailed implementation but provide pseudo code.
content.summary_of_the_review: The idea of this paper is interesting but the experiment is too weak and need to be improved.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper introduces Query by Self (QBS), which is a novel approach to active learning (AL) that is inspired from Kalman filters.The paper presents five QBS-based algorithms, a theoretical analysis, and a brief evaluation on MNIST and a regression problem (i.e., y(x) = x^2 + 100).
content.strength_and_weaknesses: The proposed approach appears to be original and might have impact in the future, but, in its current form, the paper has several critical weaknesses that must be addressed before publication. First of all, the paper is poorly written an organized. The English prose needs significant polishing, as it often-times makes the paper ambiguous or hard to understand. The paper also needs to be better organized: for example, it introduces five algorithms, of which only two are truly discussed and evaluated; the other three algorithms are simply "stranded" in the middle of the paper. Last but not least, the empirical evaluation needs major improvements. QBS must be compared against the state of the art active learners for both classification and regression. It should also be evaluated an a diverse mix of domains, rather than just MNIST and the "y(x) = X^2 + 100" problems. Without a comprehensive empirical evaluation, it is impossible to judge the papers significance and impact.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The proposed approach appears to be novel, but it is poorly written and organized (see comments above).
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper introduces a novel approach to active learning, but it requires major improvements both in writing/organization and in its empirical evaluation.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new active learning method called Query by Self. It is appropriate for both classification and regression tasks. It applies Kalman Filtering to compute the weight vector for query. The paper also provides some theoretical results of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. It proposes a new query by self method which can handle both classification and regression tasks.
2. The paper provides some theoretical analysis of the proposed method.

Weaknesses:
1. The experiments are insufficient. It conducts experiments on only one real data sets (i.e., MNIST) and one synthetic data. MNIST is not challenging enough, especially for deep neural networks. The paper should conduct experiments on more data sets, especially more challenging data sets, which can really show the performance of the proposed methods. Moreover, it only compares with vanilla Kalman filter method. It is more like an ablation study rather than a comparing experiments. The paper should compare with some state-of-the-art active learning methods to show its effectiveness or superiority.
2. The paper highlights the time complexity many times. It would be better to report the running time of the proposed method and compare it with some SOTA active learning methods.
3. The paper provides some theoretical analysis, which are good. It would be better to provide more remarks to explain the results and show why the proposed method can achieve better performance or better generalization performance.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper proposes a new query by self method and provides some theoretical results. However, the experiments are insufficient and thus it is not convincible enough to show the effectiveness. For the reproducibility, the authors seem not provide the codes.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although the paper provides some interesting methods and theoretical results, the experiments are insufficient and inconvincible.

content.title: Query by Self
content.abstract: Training with hard-to-obtain and therefore valuable data, improving generalization performance, and accelerating training speed are all challenging problems in machine learning community. Active learning , whose performance depends on its query strategy, is a powerful tool for these challenges. Unlike the famous Query by Committee strategy aimed at classification problem and dependent on a committee of student, our proposed query by self is suitable to both classification and regression problem and requires only a student,  which benefits from estimated output variance, the intermediate product of Kalman filtering optimization. This means larger scope of application and less requirement for computation and the number of data.  Besides, this strategy reduces training time and improves accuracy via filtration of similar data and better generalization.  We theoretically explain query by self strategy from the perspective of entropy. To verify effectiveness of query by self empirically, we conduct several experiments on two classical models in machine learning.
